    • getCumulativeVolumePercentAtBoilingPointKelvin

      public double getCumulativeVolumePercentAtBoilingPointKelvin(double boilingPointKelvinValue)
      Return cumulative liquid-volume recovery at a TBP boiling point in K.

      Recovery is interpolated linearly between the surrounding source-table nodes. Inputs within the qualified boundary tolerance snap to an exact source node. Extrapolation outside the complete table is rejected.

      Parameters:
      boilingPointKelvinValue - boiling point in K
      Returns:
      cumulative liquid-volume recovery in percent
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the boiling point is non-finite or outside the table

    • getTotalSpecificGravityWeightedLiquidVolumePercent

      public double getTotalSpecificGravityWeightedLiquidVolumePercent()
      Return the complete table's SG60/60-weighted liquid-volume percentage.

      This is the ideal-additive-volume mass denominator sum(Delta V_i * SG_i), with Delta V_i in liquid-volume percent. It is an auditable relative-mass term rather than a physical mass unit.

      Returns:
      complete-table SG-weighted liquid-volume percentage

    • getBoilingRangePropertiesKelvin

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.TbpBoilingRangeProperties getBoilingRangePropertiesKelvin(double lowerBoilingPointKelvin, double upperBoilingPointKelvin)
      Return the density and yield properties implied for a bounded TBP boiling range in K.

      The calculation uses the table's piecewise-linear cumulative recovery and treats each source interval specific gravity as constant. For overlap liquid-volume yields Delta V_i, the range specific gravity is sum(Delta V_i * SG_i) / sum(Delta V_i). No density-temperature correction, excess-volume model, or property correlation is applied.

      Parameters:
      lowerBoilingPointKelvin - lower boiling point in K
      upperBoilingPointKelvin - upper boiling point in K
      Returns:
      immutable boiling-range property receipt
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if either boundary is invalid or the normalized interval is not positive

    • splitAtBoilingPointsKelvin

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.TbpCutTable splitAtBoilingPointsKelvin(double... splitBoilingPointKelvin)
      Split source intervals at caller-supplied TBP boundaries in K.

      Each split point must lie strictly inside one existing interval and the points must be supplied in strictly increasing order. Liquid-volume yield is interpolated linearly with boiling temperature inside that source interval, and the source interval specific gravity is copied to both resulting subcuts. The operation therefore preserves total liquid-volume yield and implied mass on the table's ideal-additive-volume basis. It does not infer an intrainterval distillation shape, interpolate density, or estimate any other pseudo-component property.

      Parameters:
      splitBoilingPointKelvin - strictly increasing new interior TBP boundaries in K
      Returns:
      immutable finer TBP cut table
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the points are null, empty, non-finite, unordered, outside the table, or coincide with an existing boundary

    • resampleAtBoilingPointsKelvin

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.TbpCutTable resampleAtBoilingPointsKelvin(double... targetBoilingPointKelvin)
      Resample this cut table onto a caller-supplied complete TBP boundary grid in K.

      The target grid must span the source table's first and last boundaries. Cumulative liquid-volume yield is retained at existing boundaries and interpolated linearly with boiling temperature inside each source interval. Target-interval specific gravity is the liquid-volume-weighted mean of the overlapping source-interval values. The operation therefore preserves total liquid-volume yield and implied mass on the table's ideal-additive-volume basis.

      This method applies the same explicit piecewise-linear recovery and constant source-interval specific-gravity assumptions as cut splitting and adjacent re-lumping. It does not infer an intrainterval distillation shape, interpolate density with temperature, extrapolate, or estimate any other pseudo-component property.

      Parameters:
      targetBoilingPointKelvin - complete strictly increasing target TBP boundary grid in K
      Returns:
      immutable TBP cut table on the requested grid
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the grid is null, has fewer than two points, contains non-finite or unordered points, or does not span the source endpoints

    • relumpAdjacentCuts

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.TbpCutTable relumpAdjacentCuts(int... sourceCutsPerLump)
      Merge adjacent source cuts into a caller-defined sequence of coarser lumps.

      Each argument gives the number of consecutive source cuts in one output lump. Liquid-volume yield and retained TBP boundaries are copied exactly. The specific gravity of each output lump is the liquid-volume-weighted mean of its source intervals, preserving the implied mass under the same ideal-additive-volume assumption used by the assay export. This method never splits a source cut, interpolates a boundary, or estimates molecular weight or other pseudo-component properties.

      Parameters:
      sourceCutsPerLump - positive number of adjacent source cuts in each output lump
      Returns:
      immutable coarser TBP cut table
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the partition is null, empty, contains a non-positive count, or does not consume every source cut exactly once
